stops.narration: The browser posts the email and password to /login/access-token. That request is the start of the login path.
login_access_token checks the credentials, then builds a JWT. Next is the function that actually authenticates the user.
authenticate loads the account by email and checks the password. The next stop is that password check.
verify_password compares the plain password with the stored hash. If it matches, the route can return an access token.
An authenticated request arrives with the bearer token. This entry is a new request, separate from login.
get_current_user decodes the JWT and loads the user row. It depends on a database session to do that.
get_db opens a SQLModel session and hands it to the dependency. That session is what reads the user.
create_user is the admin route that accepts a new account. Next is the helper that writes the row.
The CRUD create_user hashes the password and inserts the user. Next is the hash function itself.
get_password_hash turns the plain password into an Argon2 hash before it is stored.
